title: Bit ribbons: First qualifying slip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A punch ribbon stores its active holes as the set bits of a nonnegative reading. Luz needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement bitRibbonsFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Bit counting. For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n log M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with bit counting. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [3,2,3,0,2]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 3.
The derived sequence is [1,1,1,1]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives -1.
The derived sequence is []. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives -1.

overview: Combine: Bit counting. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
